findings.issue: §1's stated evidence for D9 is refuted in §6 and neither §1 nor §13 records it. §1.5 cites JSON-LD `@context` as a format that "names a vocabulary and never carries the definition". §6.4 reads the W3C spec and shows an embedded `@context` is a carried definition and the first form the spec teaches, and §6.4 Correction 2 shows `@import` lets an embedded context dereference a remote IRI at processing time. §6.0 therefore RECOMMENDS amending D9. §13.7's "ten settled decisions, restated" carries D9 unamended and unqualified.
findings.evidence: §1.5 D9 row: "`HANDOFF…§7.1` — every self-declaring document format that succeeded (JSON-LD `@context`, the shebang line, Racket's `#lang`) names a vocabulary and never carries the definition". §6.4 Correction 1: "D9 as written forbids something the standard it cites explicitly permits ... *'The value of @context MUST be null, an IRI reference, a context definition, or an array composed of any of these.'* ... **An embedded `@context` is a carried definition, and it is the first form the spec teaches.**" §6.4 Correction 2: "**So an embedded context can dereference a remote IRI at processing time.** 'Closed' is false. 'No dereference' is false ... **do not cite JSON-LD as evidence that embedded denotations are safe.**" §6.0: "**RECOMMENDED** Amend D9 from *'a document NAMES a capability, never CARRIES one'* to *'a document may CARRY a denotation; it must only ever NAME a procedure; and it may lower its own capability, never raise it.'*"
findings.fix: §1.5 D9 "Recorded in" cell: replace the JSON-LD clause with "`HANDOFF…§7.1` — the shebang line and Racket's `#lang` name a vocabulary and never carry the definition. (**JSON-LD `@context` was cited here as a third example and §6.4 refutes it: an embedded context is a carried definition and can dereference via `@import`. Do not use JSON-LD as evidence for D9.**)" Add to the same row's consequence cell: "§6.0 RECOMMENDS amending D9 to *'may CARRY a denotation, may only NAME a procedure, may lower its own capability and never raise it'* — evidence-driven, operationally inert this cycle." §13.7 D9 row: append "**Amendment RECOMMENDED in §6.0; not yet accepted.**"

findings.section: §1 Orientation §1.4d F-ERA-1 vs §1.4b(5) and §13 §13.4 row E8
findings.issue: A pre-registered falsifier and the measurement it is supposed to test are two different ratios presented as one quantity, and the plan's own headline number is already below the threshold. F-ERA-1 fires when "the excess growth ratio drops below 1.5×" and states "It is 3.1× today" — but the 3.1× is one package (react-markdown) over the control median, while the CONFIRMED measurement two subsections earlier is the eight-parser median excess at **1.4388**. A reader applying the pre-registered threshold to the plan's own confirmed number concludes the era thesis is already dead. Separately, §1.4b(5) says the verifier reproduced every figure "to the digit" while §13.4 E8 marks the same claim reproduced **NO**.
findings.evidence: §1.4d F-ERA-1: "Excess growth ratio drops below **1.5×**. It is **3.1×** today (react-markdown ×8.75 ÷ control median ×2.81)". §1.4b(5): "Generic markdown parsers grew only **1.44×** faster than the npm registry baseline ... eight-parser median **4.0495**, fourteen-package non-markdown control median **2.8145**, excess **1.4388**." §13.4 E8: "generic markdown parsers grew only **1.44×** faster than the whole npm registry ... reproduced **NO** — **JavaScript only**". Primary source (final-gate `the-era` verification, Claim 3, verdict CONFIRMED): "Recomputed: 8-parser median = 4.0495, 14-package control median = 2.8145, excess = 1.4388 ... Every one of the 22 raw download figures reproduces to the digit."
findings.fix: §1.4d F-ERA-1: rewrite the threshold cell as "**The model-facing stack** (react-markdown, remark-gfm, rehype-raw, streamdown, remend) falls back to within **1.5×** of the 14-package npm control. It is **3.1×** today (react-markdown ×8.75 ÷ control median ×2.81). **Note this is a different quantity from §1.4b(5)'s 1.4388, which is the eight-GENERIC-parser median excess — the generic parsers are already near the baseline and that is the point of claim (5). Do not apply this threshold to 1.4388.**" §13.4 E8: change reproduced from **NO** to **PARTIAL** and set the cell to "the 22 raw figures and the 4.0495 / 2.8145 / 1.4388 arithmetic were re-derived to the digit by the area's verifier (verdict CONFIRMED); what was **not** reproduced is any non-JavaScript registry — PyPI trends were unmeasurable."

findings.issue: The 907/907 corpus gate silently degrades to a 23-file gate on any machine that is not Sagnik's, and still reports PASS. `loadCorpus()` does `if (!base || !fs.existsSync(base)) continue` for each root, and `it.skipIf(corpus.length === 0)` only skips when ALL roots are missing. On CI or a second machine the `frontmatter` root resolves via `process.cwd()` and yields 23 frontmatter-bearing files, so the suite runs, prints "23/23 identical (100.00%)", and goes green. findings.issue: The oracle's refusal counter is unreachable dead code, so every refusal is scored as BYTE-IDENTICAL. `if (back === src) { identical++ } else if (published === src && back === src) { refused++ }` — the second branch requires `back === src`, which the first branch already consumed. `refused` is structurally always 0. This directly contradicts the plan's own rule in §8 (L8406): "in the publish path a refusal is **not safe** — it is a 502 and an unpublishable note."
findings.evidence: Ran the oracle with the branch corrected to `if (published === src) { refused++; if (back === src) identical++ } else if (back === src) { identical++ }`. Result for `yamldoc`: `BYTE-IDENTICAL 284 31.31% | CHANGED 623 68.69% | THREW 0 | refused 170 18.74%` — i.e. 170 of the 284 "passes" are files the implementation declined to touch (114 real + 170 refused = 284). The shipped script reports `refused 0` and folds all 170 into the headline. For `splice` the corrected run gives `refused 0`, so today's 907/907 is genuine — but the gate cannot detect a regression into refusal.
findings.fix: Replace lines 98-101 with: `if (published === src) { refused++; if (back === src) identical++; } else if (back === src) { identical++; } else { changed++; … }` and change the VERDICT line at 137 to `const failed = changed + threw + refused`. Add to §7 F3: "The oracle must count a refusal separately from a byte-identical round trip and must FAIL on it; a writer that declines to publish is not a writer that preserves bytes."

findings.issue: The two sections prescribe incompatible implementations for the same function, and §11.4.2's version cannot meet §11.4.3's own gate. §10.6.5 rule 1 says the writer must NEVER invoke a YAML parser — which is precisely what makes the 170 unparseable files writable. §11.4.2 then instructs the builder to use eemeli/yaml's `node.range` to locate the byte range, which requires parsing with the very library that fails on those 170 files. findings.evidence: §10.6.5 rule 1, verbatim: "**WRITES NEVER PARSE.** The splice writer locates `public_slug:` (or any key) by **byte scan inside the delimiter block** and splices, or appends. It never invokes a YAML parser. This is the real fix, and it is what makes the 170 unparseable files **writable at all**." §11.4.2, verbatim: "`yaml@2.9.0` is **already a dependency** `[primary, package.json]` and exposes `node.range` on every AST node — use it to find the byte range, then throw the Document away without ever serialising it." The already-shipped `src/modules/share/domain/splice-frontmatter.ts` follows §10.6.5 (its own header: "It does not parse YAML. It scans the frontmatter block line-wise") and I measured it: it WRITES the key in 907/907 files (not merely refuses — I asserted `^public_slug: audit-test-slug$` is present in the output for all 907, including all 170), 0 refusals, 0 throws, and round-trips byte-identical 907/907.
findings.fix: Delete the `node.range` sentence from §11.4.2 entirely and replace it with: "**Do not use `yaml`'s `node.range` to find the byte span.** Reading `node.range` requires `parseDocument` to succeed, and it fails on the same 170 files that make this step necessary — a `node.range` writer tops out at 737/907 and cannot pass §11.4.3. The guard is `it.skipIf(corpus.length === 0)` (lines 173, 190) and the assertions are `expect(s.changed).toBe(0); expect(s.threw).toBe(0); expect(s.identical).toBe(s.total)` — all relative to `s.total`, never to 907. Measured per-root frontmatter counts: md=662, knowledge=222, frontmatter=23. With the two private roots absent, `process.cwd()` always exists, so corpus.length = 23, `skipIf` does NOT fire, and I ran the degraded case: gray-matter scores identical=12 changed=11 threw=0 (so the LR#68 RED-proof `expect(gm.changed + gm.threw).toBeGreaterThan(0)` still passes) and splice scores 23/23 (so the gate passes). findings.fix: Add to §11.4.3's gate block a fourth line: "The gate MUST assert its own corpus size. `test/share/frontmatter-splice.test.ts` currently guards with `it.skipIf(corpus.length === 0)`, which does not fire when the private roots are missing — `process.cwd()` always resolves, so the suite silently runs over **23** files instead of **907** and prints the identical `11 passed`. Verified by simulation: degraded run scores gray-matter 12/23 and splice 23/23, both green. **Required change:** replace the guard with `const FULL = corpus.length === 907;` plus `it.skipIf(!FULL)(…)` on both corpus tests and an explicit `expect(corpus.length).toBe(907)` inside a third test that is itself `skipIf(corpus.length === 0 || corpus.length === 23)`; and have the test print `corpus: N/907` on every run so a degraded run is visible in the log. A gate whose denominator is unasserted is not a gate."

findings.issue: Both halves of this normative instruction are false, and it directly contradicts §7.2.5, which has it right. The plan tells the builder that 170 and 171 come from two different parsers failing on two different file sets, and orders them not to be merged. Measured: the two parsers fail on the SAME 170 files — the sets are byte-for-byte identical, symmetric difference zero — and 171 is not a parse count at all.
findings.evidence: §3.1.5 verbatim: "**Note the two nearby numbers are not the same number.** 171 is the count of blocks `gray-matter` throws on; 170 is the count `yaml` cannot parse. Different parsers, different failures. Do not merge them." Measured over corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…: gray-matter `matter(src)` throws on **170** of 907; eemeli/yaml `parseDocument(...).errors.length > 0` on **170** of 907; set comparison — only-gray-matter = `[]`, only-yaml = `[]`, SETS IDENTICAL = true. The 171st file is `md/pj.md`, which parses cleanly under BOTH parsers and throws only inside `matter.stringify`, from gray-matter's re-parse of the body (gray-matter/index.js:161, verified verbatim). Contradicting section, §7.2.5, which is correct: "gray-matter throws (unpublishable → HTTP 502) | **171 = 170 parse failures + 1 stringify failure (`md/pj.md`)**" and "it fails to parse **the same 170 files**".
findings.fix: Replace the whole paragraph with: "**Note the two nearby numbers, and note that they are NOT two parsers disagreeing.** Both parsers fail on **exactly the same 170 files** — measured, symmetric difference zero. The 171st is `md/pj.md`, which parses cleanly under both and throws only inside `matter.stringify`, from gray-matter's re-parse of the body (`gray-matter/index.js:161`). So: **170 = files no YAML parser reads. 171 = 170 + `md/pj.md`, the extra one being a *serialiser* failure, not a parse failure.** Quote 170 whenever the subject is parseability and 171 only when the subject is 'what the shipped gray-matter write path throws on'. §7.2.5 states this correctly; this paragraph previously did not. findings.issue: A cross-reference names a decision id that does not exist and collides with one that does, sending a new reader to the wrong table.
findings.evidence: §1.3: 'Decision **D10.4** in the **open-decisions section** settles this: "Does MDMAX have a business model? No."' There is no section titled 'open decisions' in §13 (§13.6 is 'Contradictions inside the evidence base'); the row lives in **§12.5 'The open decisions'**, where it is numbered plainly `10.4`, alongside `W-A`, `W-B`, `W-C` and `10.1`–`10.8`. Meanwhile §1.5's table defines **D10** as 'The name is MDMAX', so a reader who follows a 'D10.4' reference into the D-namespace finds the naming decision. Confirmed by locating the row: `docs/mdmax/PLAN.md:13733`, enclosing heading `### 12.5 The open decisions` at line 13720.
findings.fix: Change §1.3 rule 2 to read: '… no separate business model. **Open decision 10.4 in §12.5** settles this: *"Does MDMAX have a business model? No."* (Note: §12.5's rows are numbered `W-A`–`W-C` and `10.1`–`10.8`; they are **not** in the `D1`–`D10` namespace of §1.5, where `D10` is the name decision.)' Add the same disambiguation as a lead-in sentence to §12.5: 'These rows are numbered `W-A`–`W-C` and `10.1`–`10.8`. They are open decisions, not the settled `D1`–`D10` of §1.5 — do not write them as `D10.4`.'

findings.evidence: §11.12.3: '| **UTF-8 integrity** | no artifact leaves a writer undecodable | swapping `perl -CSD` for `head -c`, red on a Devanagari fixture (reproduction exists: **216 bytes in, 200 out, decode error at position 198**) |' followed by 'The UTF-8 gate is ~2 hours and can land immediately.' `perl -CSD` and `head -c` appear in no file under `src/`, `test/` or `scripts/` in this repository — the incident is the `sgnk-snapshot` truncation bug recorded as Learned Rule #68 in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, outside this repo. §11's stated audience 'has never opened this repository', and therefore certainly has not read `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
findings.fix: Replace that row with a `--broke` expressed in this repository's own terms: '| **UTF-8 integrity** | no artifact leaves a writer undecodable | replacing the splice writer's `string.slice(start, end)` with a `Buffer.subarray(startByte, endByte).toString("utf8")` whose `endByte` is one byte short of a boundary — red on a Devanagari fixture, 216 bytes in / 200 out, decode error at position 198 |' and add: '(The original formulation of this gate — `perl -CSD` versus `head -c` — comes from an incident in a different repository, recorded as Learned Rule #68 in the AIOS working notes at `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
